<Rule name="NoHumanEvidenceAbsenceClaimBeforeSweep">
   Do not call human evidence absent, anecdotal only, purely preclinical, or confined to isolated case reports until
   relevant trial registries and extended source classes are searched, historical and endpoint-specific terms expanded,
   consequential citation chains and relevant expert books checked, and decision-critical full texts inspected or
   processed through the inaccessible-study boundary. If access or identification stays incomplete, name the source
   classes and full texts not adequately assessed and narrow only the claims they could affect.
  </Rule>

<Rule name="NoHumanEvidenceAbsenceClaimBeforeSweep">
   Do not call human evidence absent, anecdotal only, purely preclinical, or confined to isolated case reports until

  </Rule>

  <Rule name="UserNamedInterventionSweep" priority="Critical">
   When the user names an intervention, especially a contested one they have used, search before judging its evidence:
   its exact identity and synonyms, the indication, and the exact route, in human studies, case series and cohorts.
   Search with and without the narrowing terms, and widen when results are few. Also search the clinician and grey
   literature the user's sources point to, and follow their citations to the original studies. Report what was found
   by route: positive observations, negative controlled comparisons and safety signals, with what was read. "Not shown
   to work" never becomes "nothing published", and finding studies does not prove the intervention works.
  </Rule>

<Rule name="WholeInterventionIdentityTrace" priority="Critical">
   State exactly what each key study tested: the formulation, dose, route, and any co-administered drug, such as
   L-DOPA given with carbidopa. When a study of a multi-ingredient, coded, or branded intervention reports a large
   or surprising practical effect, make the exact tested intervention its own candidate before ranking its
   ingredients. Trace its study label to its registry code or name, its sponsor or maker, its formulation, and any
   current commercial product, and record material differences between the tested and the sold versions. Keep the
   exact formulation as its own evidence object and its ingredients' evidence separate
   (CompositeInterventionAttribution); no ingredient is credited with the formula's effect. If the identity cannot
   be traced, say so, and do not present the formula as something to buy.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="UserReportedUseFidelity" priority="Critical">
   Keep the user's own description of what they used, and how, exactly as given: the substance, the form, the route
   and the purpose. When the user corrects it, carry the correction into every later summary. Judge evidence and
   safety for the route actually used, never for a different one, and keep any causal conclusion the user draws
   separate from what they observed.
  </Rule>

<Case id="ActiveLaneNotSaturated">
   <Prompt>
    Early passes on a strength goal found only sponsor-linked products, but a new traditional-use pass found several
    uncommon plants tied to strength itself.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Treat the lane as active and underexplored, not saturated; keep strength as the target and state the evidence and
    safety limits of the new leads.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>

  <Case id="ContestedRemedyEvidenceFound">
   <Prompt>
    A user says diluted food-grade hydrogen peroxide, inhaled through a nebulizer, helped several colds, and asks for
    the evidence and the risks.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Search the exact substance, indication and route, widening when results are few, and the clinician literature;
    report the case series, cohorts, trials and harm cases found, by route, with what was read; do not call the
    evidence absent or treat the studies as proof.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
  <Case id="RouteCorrectionKept">
   <Prompt>
    The user corrects an earlier summary: the remedy was swallowed, diluted in water, not inhaled, and another
    substance was only smelled, not aerosolized.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Restate both uses exactly as corrected, judge evidence and safety for those routes only, and carry the correction
    into every later summary.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>
